docs.title: Selenium Grid and Parallel Testing
docs.text:
Selenium Grid allows running WebDriver scripts on remote machines to enable parallel testing and cross-browser testing.

  • Goals:

    • Run tests in parallel on multiple machines.
    • Test on different browser versions.
    • Enable cross-platform testing.

  • Setup:

    1. Prerequisites:

      • Java 11 or higher installed.
      • Browsers installed.
      • Browser drivers:
        • Selenium Manager (recommended): java -jar selenium-server-<version>.jar standalone --selenium-manager true
        • Manually installed and added to PATH.
      • Selenium Server JAR file (download from latest release).

    2. Start the Grid: bash java -jar selenium-server-<version>.jar standalone

    3. Point WebDriver Tests:

      • Configure WebDriver to connect to http://localhost:4444.

    4. (Optional) Check Grid Status:

      • Open http://localhost:4444 in a browser.

  • Configure WebDriver:

    ```csharp public IWebDriver GetRemoteWebDriver(BrowserType browserType) { IWebDriver driver;

    switch (browserType)
{
    case BrowserType.ChromeDriver:
        driver = new RemoteWebDriver(_testsetting.GridUri, new ChromeOptions());
        break;
    case BrowserType.EdgeDriver:
        driver = new RemoteWebDriver(_testsetting.GridUri, new EdgeOptions());
        break;
    case BrowserType.FireFoxDriver:
        driver = new RemoteWebDriver(_testsetting.GridUri, new FirefoxOptions());
        break;
    default:
        driver = new RemoteWebDriver(_testsetting.GridUri, new ChromeOptions());
        break;
}

return driver;

    } ```

docs.title: What is SpecFlow?
docs.text:
• SpecFlow is a Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) framework for .NET, similar to Cucumber.
  • It uses Gherkin, a plain-text language, which supports over 70 languages.
  • It is cross-platform, running on macOS, Linux, and Windows.
  • SpecFlow integrates with popular IDEs like Visual Studio, VS Code, and Rider.

docs.title: Why Use SpecFlow?
docs.text:
• SpecFlow uses simple English language, enabling clear communication between QAs, developers, BAs, and POs.
  • It fosters a shared understanding across the team.
  • It aids in documenting the entire Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC).

docs.title: SpecFlow Ecosystem
docs.text:
The SpecFlow ecosystem supports the entire SDLC, from requirements gathering to project delivery.

Role Tool/Feature Business Analyst, Product Owner SpecFlow Online Gherkin Editor Developers, QA Leads, Automation Testers SpecFlow plugins for IDEs DevOps/QA/Developers Azure DevOps SpecFlow LivingDoc Client (Stakeholder) SpecFlow LivingDoc (offline/hosted)

docs.title: SpecFlow in the SDLC
docs.text:
• Requirement Gathering:
    • Gherkin Language:
      • Purpose: Write requirements in plain English using the Given-When-Then format.
      • Benefit: Ensures all stakeholders understand the requirements.
    • Collaboration:
      • Tools: Integrates with Azure DevOps and Git.
      • Benefit: Facilitates collaboration between BAs, developers, and testers.
  • Development:
    • SpecFlow:
      • Integration: Works with Visual Studio and other .NET tools.
      • Functionality: Converts Gherkin scenarios into executable code.
    • SpecFlow+ Runner:
      • Purpose: Advanced test execution and reporting.
      • Benefit: Provides detailed insights and control over test runs.
  • Testing:
    • Automated Testing:
      • CI/CD Integration: Supports automated acceptance tests in CI/CD pipelines.
      • Benefit: Ensures consistent test execution.
    • SpecFlow+ LivingDoc:
      • Purpose: Generates living documentation from feature files.
      • Benefit: Keeps documentation up-to-date.
  • Project Delivery:
    • Continuous Feedback:
      • Tools: SpecFlow+ LivingDoc and SpecMap.
      • Benefit: Provides continuous feedback on requirements and tests.
    • Documentation:
      • LivingDoc: Keeps stakeholders informed with up-to-date documentation.
      • Benefit: Ensures the final product meets requirements.

docs.title: Feature Files and Components
docs.text:
Feature: Checkout Process
  As a customer
  I want to complete a purchase
  So that I can receive my ordered items

  Background:
    Given I am logged in to the e-commerce website
    And my shopping cart is empty

  Scenario: Add Items to Cart
    Given I am on the product page
    When I add "Product A" to my cart
    And I add "Product B" to my cart
    Then my cart should contain 2 items

  Scenario Outline: Checkout with Different Payment Methods
    Given my cart contains "<item_count>" items
    When I proceed to checkout
    And I select "<payment_method>" as payment method
    Then I should receive a confirmation email

    Examples:
      | item_count | payment_method  |
      | 1          | Credit Card     |
      | 2          | PayPal          |
      | 3          | Bank Transfer   |
  • Feature: Defines the feature being tested. Provides a high-level description.
  • Scenario: Outlines a specific test case or scenario. Describes a sequence of steps.
  • Scenario Outline: Used for multiple data sets for the same scenario. Uses placeholders for input values.
  • Background: Defines steps executed before each scenario. Avoids repeating setup steps.

docs.title: Working with SpecFlow Tables
docs.text: SpecFlow's Table object represents tabular data from feature files.

docs.title: Data Table:
docs.text:
Passes multiple values or records into step definitions.

Scenario: Add multiple users
  Given I have the following users
    | FirstName | LastName  |
    | John      | Doe       |
    | Jane      | Smith     |
  When I add these users to the system
  Then I should see these users in the user list

** Accessing data tables

[Given(@"I have the following users")]
public void GivenIHaveTheFollowingUsers(Table table)
{
    foreach (var row in table.Rows)
    {
        string firstName = row["FirstName"];
        string lastName = row["LastName"];
        Console.WriteLine($"FirstName: {firstName}, LastName: {lastName}");
    }
}

  Then I should see the dashboard for "<username>"

  Examples:
    | username | password |

    | user2    | pass2    |

Using CreateDynamicInstance(): Creates a dynamic object from a single table row.

Scenario: Create a product from a single row table
  Given I have the following product

Using CreateDynamicSet():

Creates a collection of dynamic objects from table rows.

docs.title: SpecFlow Hooks
docs.text:
• Hooks are methods that run at specific points in the test execution lifecycle.
  • Used for setup, teardown, and configuration.
  • Common hook types: BeforeTestRun, AfterTestRun, BeforeFeature, AfterFeature, BeforeScenario, AfterScenario, BeforeStep, AfterStep.
using TechTalk.SpecFlow;

namespace LWASpecflow.Hooks
{
    [Binding]
    public sealed class TestInitializer
    {
        [BeforeScenario("@tag1")]
        public void BeforeScenariowithTag() { }

        [BeforeScenario(Order = 1)]
        public void FirstBeforeScenario() { }

        [BeforeScenario]
        public void BeforeScenario() { }

        [BeforeTestRun]
        public static void BeforeTestRun() { }

        [AfterScenario]
        public void AfterScenario() { }
    }
}
  • BeforeFeature/AfterFeature and BeforeTestRun/AfterTestRun methods must be static.

docs.title: Working with Tables (Single and Multiple Columns)

Scenario: List of single column data

docs.title: Extent Reporting with SpecFlow
docs.text:
• Extent Reports supports BDD frameworks.

  • Steps:

  • Install ExtentReports package.
  • Add FeatureContext for feature details in hooks class.
  • Initialize ExtentReports in hooks class.
[BeforeTestRun]
public static void InitializeExtentReports()
{
    var reportPath = Path.GetDirectoryName(Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly().Location) + "TestReport.html";
    _extentReports = new ExtentReports();
    var SparkReport = new ExtentSparkReporter(reportPath);
    _extentReports.AttachReporter(SparkReport);
}
  1. Flush the report after test run.
[AfterTestRun]
public static void closeExtentReports()
{
    _extentReports.Flush();
}

docs.title: Creating Extent Report UI with Step Definitions
docs.text:
Defining and Logging in Reports in hook files.

[BeforeScenario()]
public void InitializeDriver()
{
    var feature = _extentReports.CreateTest<Feature>(_featureContext.FeatureInfo.Title);
    _scenario = feature.CreateNode<Scenario>(_scenarioContext.ScenarioInfo.Title);
}

[AfterStep]
public void AfterTestSteps()
{
    if (_scenarioContext.TestError == null)
    {
        switch (_scenarioContext.StepContext.StepInfo.StepDefinitionType)
        {
            case TechTalk.SpecFlow.Bindings.StepDefinitionType.Given:
                _scenario.CreateNode<Given>(_scenarioContext.StepContext.StepInfo.Text);
                break;
            case TechTalk.SpecFlow.Bindings.StepDefinitionType.When:
                _scenario.CreateNode<Given>(_scenarioContext.StepContext.StepInfo.Text);
                break;
            case TechTalk.SpecFlow.Bindings.StepDefinitionType.Then:
                _scenario.CreateNode<Given>(_scenarioContext.StepContext.StepInfo.Text);
                break;
        }
    }
    else
    {
        switch (_scenarioContext.StepContext.StepInfo.StepDefinitionType)
        {
            case TechTalk.SpecFlow.Bindings.StepDefinitionType.Given:
                _scenario.CreateNode<Given>(_scenarioContext.StepContext.StepInfo.Text).Fail();
                break;
            case TechTalk.SpecFlow.Bindings.StepDefinitionType.When:
                _scenario.CreateNode<Given>(_scenarioContext.StepContext.StepInfo.Text).Fail();
                break;
            case TechTalk.SpecFlow.Bindings.StepDefinitionType.Then:
                _scenario.CreateNode<Given>(_scenarioContext.StepContext.StepInfo.Text).Fail();
                break;
        }
    }
}

docs.title: JavaScriptExecutor in Selenium
docs.text:
• JavaScriptExecutor allows executing JavaScript code in the browser context.
  • Useful for operations not directly supported by Selenium.
  • Provides two methods ExecuteScript and ExecuteAsyncScript.

docs.title: steps to use:
docs.text:
1. Import the package: import org.openqa.selenium.JavascriptExecutor;
  2. Create a reference: JavascriptExecutor js = (JavascriptExecutor)driver;
  3. Call the method: js.executeScript(script, args);

docs.title: ExecuteScript
docs.text:
Executes JavaScript in the current window or frame. Returns values of types: WebElement, List, String, Long, Boolean.

using OpenQA.Selenium;
using OpenQA.Selenium.Chrome;

class Program
{
    static void Main()
    {
        IWebDriver driver = new ChromeDriver();
        driver.Navigate().GoToUrl("[https://example.com](https://example.com)");
        IJavaScriptExecutor js = (IJavaScriptExecutor)driver;

        IWebElement elementToScrollTo = driver.FindElement(By.Id("elementId"));
        js.ExecuteScript("arguments[0].scrollIntoView(true);", elementToScrollTo);

        js.ExecuteScript("arguments[0].style.backgroundColor = 'yellow';", elementToScrollTo);

        string title = (string)js.ExecuteScript("return document.title;");
        Console.WriteLine("Page Title: " + title);

        IWebElement button = driver.FindElement(By.Id("buttonId"));
        js.ExecuteScript("arguments[0].click();", button);

        IWebElement inputField = driver.FindElement(By.Id("inputFieldId"));
        js.ExecuteScript("arguments[0].value='New Value';", inputField);

        driver.Quit();
    }
}

docs.title: Xpath
docs.text:
1. What is XPath? A query language which is used to find a node or set of nodes in XML/HTML document

  2. Absolute and Relative Xpath: 

    1. Absolute XPath: Uses the complete path starting from root (/html) to desired element       
      Syntax: /html/body/div[2]/div/...

2. Combination of Relative and Absolute XPath         
      Example: //span[@id='u123']/div[1]/a

docs.title: Relative Xpath
docs.text:
1. Relative XPath Using Node Attributes

        Syntax:
    //TagName[@Attribute Name="Attribute Value"]

  2. Relative XPath Using Text 

        Syntax:
    //TagName[text()="Text"]

  3. Dynamic Elements: Elements with dynamic property-values and/or text 

      1. Using 'and' Operator
     Syntax: 
     //TagName[@Att1='Value1' and @Att2='Value2']
     //TagName[@Att='Value' and Text()='Value']

  2. Using 'or' Operator
      Syntax: 
     //TagName[@Att1='Value1' or @Att2='Value2']
     //TagName[@Att='Value' or Text()='Value']

  3. Using 'contains'
     Syntax:
     //TagName[contains(@Att,'Partial Value')]
     //TagName[contains(text(),'Partial Value')]

  4. Using 'starts-with' 
      Syntax:
     //TagName[starts-with(@Att,'Starting Value')]
     //TagName[starts-with(text(),'Starting Value')]

  5. Hybrid
      Syntax:
      //TagName[contains(@Att1,'Partial Value') and starts-with(text(),'Starting Value')]  
      //TagName[@Att1='Value' or starts-with(@Att2,'Starting Value')]
      //*[@Att='Value']

  4. XPath Axes: 

    a. Parent and Child Relation         
    Syntax:           
    //Node1/child::*          
    //Node1/parent::*

b. Ancestor and Descendant Relationship       
    Syntax:       
    //Node1/ancestor::*       
    //Node1/descendant::*

c. Preceding and Following        
    Syntax:       
    //Node1/preceding::*          
    //Node1/preceding-sibling::*          
    //Node1/following::*          
    //Node1/following-sibling::*

docs.title: CSS selector:
docs.text:
1. What is CSS and CSS Selector? CSS (Cascading Style Sheets): Describes presentation of elements mentioned in HTML CSS Selector: Pointer for applying the styling mentioned in CSS

  2. Creating CSS Selector Using Attributes

    Syntax: TagName[Att1=Value]
In case Att1 is 'id' or 'class' then we can use following symbols:
    id => # (hash)
    class => . (dot)
Examples: 1. div#u123   2. span.layerParent

  3. Creating CSS Selectors for Dynamic Elements

      1. Using partial value of attribute (Symbol - *)
      Example: TagName[Att1*='Partial Value']

  2. Using starting value of attribute (Symbol ^)
      Example: TagName[Att1^='Starting Value']

  3. Using ending value of attribute (Symbol $)
      Example: TagName[Att1$='Ending Value']

  4. Creating CSS with Multiple Attributes

      a. ANDING the Attributes (No Symbol Required)
      Syntax: TagName[Att1=Value][Att2=Value]

  b. ORING the Attributes (',' will work as 'OR')
      Syntax: TagName[Att1=Value], TagName[Att2=Value]

  5. Advanced CSS Selectors

      1. Using only TagName and Attribute Name

  2. Node1,Node2 => Matches all Node1s and Node2s

  3. Node1 Node2 => Matches all Node2s which are descendant of Node1

  4. Node1>Node2 => Matches all Node2s which are children of Node1

  5. Node1+Node2 => Matches sibling Node2 placed immediately after Node1

  6. Node1~Node2 => Matches all sibling Node2s placed after Node1

  6. using Node Child Numbering 

      1. Node1:first-child 
      => Selects all Node1s who are first child of their parent

  2. Node1:last-child 
     => Selects all Node1s who are last child of their parent

  3. Node1:nth-child(n) 
     => Selects all Node1s who are nth child of their parent

docs.title: What is SelectorsHub?
docs.text: SelectorsHub is a free-to-use browser extension that auto-suggests all the possible combinations of attributes, text, siblings, etc. to build selectors within seconds.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
SelectorsHub offers unique features that make it one of the best XPath tools available.

  1. Auto Suggest:

    SelectorsHub is an open-source browser extension that auto-suggests all possible combinations of attributes, text, siblings, etc., to build selectors within seconds.

  2. Compiler for Selectors

    Previously, no tool could indicate what was wrong with a selector. Developers had to become experts to understand their mistakes. DevTools would only suggest 0 matching nodes for an incorrect selector pattern. Now, SelectorsHub provides a Selector Compiler that displays correct error messages and highlights incorrect or missing elements in the selector.

  3. ShadowDOM Support

    SelectorsHub allows writing and verifying CSS Selectors for ShadowDOM elements. Users can inspect and verify selectors for ShadowDOM elements.

  4. iFrame Support

    SelectorsHub helps identify whether an inspected element is inside an iframe.

  5. SVG Element Support

    SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics) elements require different XPath patterns. SelectorsHub assists in identifying the correct format while inspecting SVG elements.

docs.title: Introduction to Selenium
docs.text:
Selenium is a powerful testing tool used to automate test scripts for web applications across various browsers and platforms. It does not support desktop applications.

You can download Selenium from www.seleniumhq.org.

docs.title: Significance of Selenium
docs.text:
• Open-source: It's a free and open-source tool for web application testing.
  • Cross-platform and multi-language support: It supports executing scripts on various operating systems and in major programming languages like C#, Ruby, Java, Python, Perl, and JavaScript.
  • Cross-browser testing: It enables executing scripts across different browsers.

docs.title: Selenium Components
docs.text:
Selenium consists of the following components:

  • Selenium IDE (Integrated Development Environment)
  • Selenium RC (Remote Control)
  • Selenium WebDriver
  • Selenium Grid

docs.title: Selenium IDE
docs.text:
• Selenium IDE is a record-and-playback tool, available as an add-on for Firefox and Chrome.
  • It allows recording user interactions and playing them back as test scripts.
  • Recorded scripts can be exported to various programming languages like Java, C#, Ruby, and Python.

docs.title: Selenium RC (Selenium 1.0)
docs.text:
• Selenium RC (Remote Control), also known as Selenium 1.0, was the core Selenium framework before WebDriver.
  • It supports web browsers that can interpret HTTP requests and doesn't require browser-specific drivers.
  • It uses a Selenium server to start, stop, and control browsers automatically.
  • Disadvantage: Requires a running RC server to execute test scripts.
  • Components: Script -> Selenium Server -> Application/Browser
  • Setup:
    1. Download the Selenium server JAR file.
    2. Run the server.
    3. Execute the script.
    4. Example code: driver = new RemoteWebDriver(_testsetting.GridUri, new ChromeOptions());

docs.title: Selenium Grid
docs.text:
• Selenium Grid is designed for running test scripts in parallel across multiple test environments, browsers, operating systems, and machines.
  • The central machine controlling the tests is called the "hub," and the remote machines executing the tests are called "nodes."
  • Primarily used for performance testing.

docs.title: Selenium WebDriver
docs.text:
• Selenium WebDriver enables creating and executing test cases using element/object locators.
  • It interacts directly with the web browser without an external server, making it faster than Selenium RC.

docs.title: 🚀 Selenium Automation Flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD;
     A([Start]) --> B[📦 Import Language Bindings]
    B --> C[🌐 Import Selenium WebDriver]
    C --> D[🚗 Create Driver Instance]
    D --> E[🔗 Send HTTP GET Request]
    E --> F[📄 Fetch Web Page]
    F --> G{✅ Is Page Title Correct?}
    G -- Yes --> H[📊 Print Success Status]
    G -- No --> I[❌ Print Failure Status]
    H & I --> J[❌ Close & Exit]
    J --> K([End])

docs.title: Selenium Commands
docs.text:
Selenium commands are used to automate web browser interactions. They can be categorized as follows:

  1. Application Commands: (Less common, often configuration related)
  2. Conditional Commands: (Used for control flow, e.g., if, else)
  3. Browser Commands: (Control the browser itself)
  4. Navigational Commands: (Navigate within the browser)
  5. Wait Commands: (Handle synchronization)

docs.title: Browser Commands
docs.text:
These commands control the browser's behavior.

Commands Description Driver.Navigate().GoToUrl("https://google.com") Open the URL in the browser. Driver.URL = "https://google.com" Open the URL in the browser. Driver.Manage().Window.Maximize() Maximize the browser window. Driver.Manage().Window.Minimize() Minimize the browser window. Driver.Manage().Timeouts().ImplicitWait = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10) Set implicit wait timeout. Driver.Navigate().Back() Navigate to the previous page. Driver.Navigate().Forward() Navigate to the next page. Driver.Navigate().Refresh() Refreshes the current page. Driver.Quit() Closes the browser and ends session. Driver.close() Close the current browser window.

docs.title: Element Interaction
docs.text:
These commands interact with web elements.

Commands Description Driver.findElement(By locator) Find the element by its locator. Driver.findelements(By locator) Find all elements by its locator. Element.click() Click on the element. Element.SendKeys("text") Type text into the input field. Element.clear() Clear the content of a text field. Element.Submit() Submit a form. Element.GerAttribute("attributeName") Retrieves the value of an attribute. Element.GetCssValue("color") Get CSS property value of an element. Element.GetText() Retrieves the text content. Element.Displayd Check if the element is visible. Element.Enabled Check if the element is enabled. Element.Selected Check if a checkbox or radio button is selected.

docs.title: Handling Alerts and Pop-Ups
docs.text:
These commands manage browser alerts or pop-ups.

Commands Description IAlert alert = Driver.SwitchTo().Alert(); Switches to the alert window. alert.Accept(); Accept the alert (OK button). alert.Dismiss(); Dismiss the alert (Cancel button). alert.GetText(); Retrieves the text from the alert. alert.SendKeys("input text") Send the text to the alert.

docs.title: Navigation and Frame Handling
docs.text:
These commands switch between windows, frames, or iframes.

Commands Description String mainWindowHandle = driver.CurrentWindowHandle; Retrieve the handle of the current window. Driver.SwitchTo().Window("windowName"); Switch to a specific browser window. IReadOnlyCollection<string> allWindowHandles = driver.WindowHandles; Get a list of all open windows. Driver.SwitchTo().Frame("framename"); Switches to a frame or iframe by name. Driver.SwitchTo().Frame(frameID); Switches to a frame or iframe by ID. driver.SwitchTo().Frame(frameWebElement); Switches to a frame or iframe by element. Driver.SwitchTo().ParentFrame(); Switches back to the parent frame. Driver.SwitchTo().DefaultContent(); Switches back to the main page content.

Thread.Sleep(3000); Halts execution (not recommended).

docs.title: Locators in Selenium
docs.text: A locator is an address that uniquely identifies a web element within a webpage. Locators are the HTML properties of a web element that tell Selenium which element to perform an action on.

docs.title: Different Types of Web Elements
docs.text:
The most common elements are:

  • Text box
  • Button
  • Drop Down
  • Hyperlink
  • Check Box
  • Radio Button
  • Timestamp
  • Popup and alert

docs.title: Type of locators:
CSS selector Locators
docs.text:
1. Tag & id: Use hash (#) to join the both attribute

    csharp driver.find_element(By.CSS_SELECTOR,'input#email').send_keys('abhisheksinghcpj@gmail.com'); // or driver.find_element(By.CSS_SELECTOR, '#email').clear(); //for C# driver.FindElement(By.CssSelector("input#email")).send_keys('abhisheksinghcpj@gmail.com');

  2. Tag & class: Use dot (.) to join the both attribute

    csharp driver.find_element(By.CSS_SELECTOR,'input.inputtext').send_keys('abhishekcpj@gmail.com');

  3. Tag & attribute: Use square bracket [] to join attribute

    csharp driver.find_element(By.CSS_SELECTOR,'input[placeholder="Password"]').send_keys('abc123456');

  4. Tag, class & attribute

    csharp driver.find_element(By.CSS_SELECTOR,'button._42ft[type="submit"]').click();

  5. Advance CSS Selector

    • Direct Child Selector (>): .parent > .child
    • Adjacent Sibling Selector (+): .sibling1 + .sibling2
    • General Sibling Selector (~): .sibling1 ~ .sibling2
    • Attribute Selector ([]): input[type='text']
    • ID Selector (#): #myId
    • Class Selector (.): .myClass
    • Universal Selector (*): div *
    • Pseudo-classes and Pseudo-elements: a:hover, ::before

docs.title: Selenium XPath
docs.text: XPath is a query language for selecting nodes from a web page using XML expressions. By using XPath, we can locate any element on a web page that has an HTML DOM structure.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
//tagname[@attribute='value']

In the above syntax:

  • //: Selects nodes in the document from the current node that match the selection no matter where they are.
  • tagname: The name of the tag of a particular node.
  • @: Selects attributes.
  • attribute: The name of the attribute of the node.
  • value: The value of the attribute.

docs.title: Types of XPath
docs.text:
XPath is categorized into two main types:

  1. Absolute XPath: The XPath starts from the root of the HTML page.

    • Syntax: /html/body/tag1[index]/tag2[index]/.../tagN[index]
    • Example: /html/body/div[2]/div/div[2]/div/div/div/fieldset/form/div[1]/input[1]

  2. Relative XPath: The path starts from the middle of the DOM structure.

    • Syntax: //htmltag[@attribute1='value1' and @attribute2='value2']
    • Example: //input[@id='passwd' and @placeholder='password']

docs.title: XPath Options
docs.text: We use different options like AND, OR, contains(), text(), and starts-with().

docs.title: AND / OR
docs.text: driver.FindElement(By.XPath("//input[@name='keyword' and @placeholder='Search products & brands']")).SendKeys("laptops");

docs.title: contains()
docs.text: A built-in method used to locate an element based on a partial text match (any text of the whole value). //[contains(@attribute_name, 'attribute_value')]

docs.title: starts-with()
docs.text: The starts-with() function is used to find the element whose attribute value changes (e.g., message12, message15, message28) on refresh or any operation on the webpage, but the initial text remains the same. //input[starts-with(@attribute_name, 'attribute_partial_value')]

docs.title: text()
docs.text: Used to find any text value inside the start and end tag (text that appears on the front screen). //tagName[text()='abhi']

docs.title: XPath Attributes
docs.text:
XPath attributes are recommended when you don't have a suitable id or name attribute for the element you want to locate.

Expression Description nodeName Selects all nodes with this name / Selects from the root node // Selects nodes in the document from the current node that match the selection no matter where they are. . Selects the current node @ Selects attributes .. Selects the parent of the current node * Selects any element node @* Selects any attribute node node() Selects any node /audio/file[last()] Selects the last audio file that is a child of an audio element /audio/file[1] Selects the first audio file /audio/file[position()>4] Selects all audio files that are children of an audio file and have a position greater than 4. //[@labeled] Selects all elements with the labeled attribute. /audio/file/[price>9.99]/title Selects all the title elements of the file element of the audio element with a price greater than 9.99.

docs.title: XPath Axes
docs.text:
XPath axes are used to search for multiple nodes in an XML document from the current node context. These methods are mainly used when the web element cannot be identified using ID, name, class name, link text, CSS selector, and XPath locators.

Syntax: XPath = XPath(Current node)//xpath_axes::tagName

var preceding = driver.FindElements(By.XPath("//a[@id='challenges-link']/parent::li/preceding::*"));
  • self: //self::tagName
  • parent: //parent::tagName
  • child
  • ancestor: Parent of parent
  • descendant: Child of child
  • following
  • following-sibling
  • preceding
  • preceding-sibling
  • following nodes are the nodes below/after the current node in the HTML code.
  • following-sibling nodes are all nodes parallel and below the current node.
  • preceding nodes are the nodes above/before the current node in the HTML code.
  • We can use * as the tagName if we don't know it clearly.
using OpenQA.Selenium;
using OpenQA.Selenium.Chrome;
using OpenQA.Selenium.Support.UI;
using System;
using System.Collections.ObjectModel;

public class XPathExample
{
    public static void Main(string[] args)
    {
        IWebDriver driver = new ChromeDriver();
        driver.Manage().Window.Maximize();
        driver.Navigate().GoToUrl("[https://owasp.org/www-project-juice-shop/](https://owasp.org/www-project-juice-shop/)");

        string x = driver.FindElement(By.XPath("//a[@id='challenges-link']")).Text;
        Console.WriteLine("display the value for selected path:-> " + x);

        // 1. self axes
        string x1 = driver.FindElement(By.XPath("//a[@id='challenges-link']//self::a")).Text;
        Console.WriteLine("self axes:-> " + x1);

        // parent node
        string p = driver.FindElement(By.XPath("//a[@id='challenges-link']//parent::*")).Text;
        Console.WriteLine("parent axes:-> " + p);

        // ancestor node
        string a = driver.FindElement(By.XPath("//a[@id='challenges-link']//ancestor::ul")).Text;
        Console.WriteLine("ancestor axes:-> " + a);

        // child node
        string c = driver.FindElement(By.XPath("//a[@id='challenges-link']//ancestor::ul/child::li")).Text;
        Console.WriteLine("child node of ancestor axes ->" + c);

        // descendant : child of child node
        ReadOnlyCollection<IWebElement> d = driver.FindElements(By.XPath("//a[@id='challenges-link']/ancestor::ul/descendant::*"));
        Console.WriteLine("lengthe descendant node value :-> " + d.Count);

        // following
        ReadOnlyCollection<IWebElement> folwng = driver.FindElements(By.XPath("//a[@id='challenges-link']//parent::li//following::li"));
        Console.WriteLine("following length ->" + folwng.Count);
        folwng = driver.FindElements(By.XPath("//a[@id='challenges-link']//parent::li//following::*"));
        Console.WriteLine("following node length having tag * ->" + folwng.Count);

        // following-sibling
        ReadOnlyCollection<IWebElement> fs = driver.FindElements(By.XPath("//a[@id='challenges-link']//parent::li//following-sibling::li"));
        Console.WriteLine("following-sibling length ->" + fs.Count);

        // preceding node
        ReadOnlyCollection<IWebElement> preceding = driver.FindElements(By.XPath("//a[@id='challenges-link']//parent::li//preceding::*"));
        Console.WriteLine("lengthe of preceding node -> " + preceding.Count);

        // preceding-sibling node
        ReadOnlyCollection<IWebElement> preceding_sb = driver.FindElements(By.XPath("//a[@id='challenges-link']//parent::li//preceding-sibling::*"));
        Console.WriteLine("lengthe of preceding-sibling node -> " + preceding_sb.Count);

        System.Threading.Thread.Sleep(5000);
        driver.Quit();
    }
}

docs.title: XPath Syntax summary
docs.text:
XPath is used to locate elements on a web page.

  1. Basic Syntax: //tagName[@attribute='value']
  2. Concatenation: //tagName[@attribute='value'][@attribute='value']
  3. Attribute Starts With: //tagName[starts-with(@attribute,'value')]
  4. Attribute Contains Text: //tagName[contains(@attribute,'value')]
  5. Text Value: //tagName[text()='value']
  6. Text Contains Text: //tagName[contains(text(),'partialValue')]
  7. Parent Element: //tagName[@attribute='value']/..
  8. Parent Tag: //tagName[@attribute='value']/parent::tagName
  9. Following Sibling: //tagName[@attribute='value']/following-sibling::tagName
  10. Preceding Sibling: //tagName[@attribute='value']/preceding-sibling::tagName

docs.title: 1. What is automation testing, and why is it important?
docs.text:
Automation testing is a process of using automation software tools to write a script to perform test cases such as entering data and comparing the results, etc. is known as Automation testing. The goal of Automation Testing is to reduce the number of test cases to be run manually so we can reduce human efforts. It is essential for repetitive and time-consuming test scenarios, ensuring quicker feedback and improving test coverage.

Benefits:

  • Speed: Automated tests execute faster than manual tests, which accelerates the testing process.
  • Reusability: Test scripts can be reused across different versions of an application.
  • Consistency: Automation eliminates human error, ensuring consistent test execution.
  • Coverage: Automation allows for running a large number of test cases in a short period, covering more scenarios.
  • Efficiency: It frees up testers to focus on more complex testing tasks by handling repetitive test cases.

docs.title: 2. How to Maintain Automation Script:
docs.text:
Automation scripts are a powerful tool, saving you time and reducing errors. But they are not set-and-forget. Regular maintenance is essential to keep them running smoothly and adapt to changing requirements.

  1. Documentation is Your Best Friend:

    • Start with thorough documentation.
    • Properly document your automation script, detailing its purpose, inputs, outputs, and dependencies.
    • This documentation will be invaluable for future reference and for helping other team members understand and work with the script.

  2. Version Control:

    • Use version control systems like Git to manage your automation script. This enables you to track changes, collaborate with others, and easily roll back to previous versions if issues arise.
    • Create branches for new features or bug fixes and merge them when they are stable.

  3. Regular Testing:

    • Automation scripts can break when systems change, and they need to adapt. Implement automated tests to regularly validate the functionality of your scripts.
    • This allows for easier maintenance and reusability.
    • These tests should check for expected outputs and flag any discrepancies.

  4. Code Base:

    • Follow a code base and naming conventions for your scripts.
    • Use comments to explain complex logic and document important decisions.

  5. Continuous Integration (CI):

    • Integrate your automation script into your CI/CD pipeline. Automated building and testing of code to ensure it works correctly within the shared codebase.
    • Rapid feedback to developers on the status of their code changes.
    • This ensures that changes are tested and deployed automatically with each code change to quickly identify regressions, reducing manual intervention and ensuring that the script remains compatible with the latest software updates.

  6. Docker:

    • Docker containers encapsulate the testing environment, ensuring that test scripts run consistently, regardless of the host system’s configuration.
    • Test environments can be easily shared between developers and integrated into CI/CD pipelines, ensuring that the same environment is used for testing at every stage.
    • Docker containers are lightweight and start quickly, allowing for rapid scaling of test automation processes.
    • Docker for test script automation, you can create and manage isolated, consistent testing environments, making it easier to develop, execute, and maintain automated tests as part of your CI/CD pipeline.

  7. Parameterization:

    • Avoid hardcoding values whenever possible.
    • Use configuration files or external data sources for test data.

  8. Page Object Model (POM):

    • Implement the Page Object Model to separate page elements from test scripts.
    • Changes in the UI won’t affect your tests as much.

  9. Error Handling:

    • Create robust error-handling mechanisms within your script.
    • By logging errors and exceptions, you’ll be able to diagnose issues quickly and make necessary adjustments.
    • Use explicit waits for elements rather than hard-coded sleeps.

  10. Keep Software Dependencies Updated:

    • Regularly update and maintain the libraries and dependencies your automation script relies on.
    • Outdated dependencies can lead to vulnerabilities and compatibility issues.
    • This ensures compatibility with new browser versions and security updates.

  11. Test Maintenance:

    • Update tests to reflect changes in the application.
    • Automated tests should evolve with the application’s features.

  12. Regression Testing:

    • Continuously run regression tests to catch issues early.
    • Prioritize and select a subset of test cases for faster feedback.

  13. Test Data Management:

    • Keep test data separate from test scripts and manage it effectively.
    • Consider using data factories or generators to create test data.

  14. Training and Knowledge Sharing:

    • Ensure that team members are trained and knowledgeable about the testing framework and best practices.
    • Share information about changes and updates within the team.

  15. Monitor Performance:

    • Set up performance monitoring to track how your script performs over time.
    • This can help identify slowdowns or bottlenecks, allowing you to optimize the script for efficiency.

  16. Review and Refactor:

    • Periodically review your automation script’s code for redundancies and inefficiencies.
    • Refactoring can make your script cleaner and more maintainable.

  17. Plan for Scalability:

    • Consider future growth when designing your script. Ensure it can easily adapt to increased data or user demands without major overhauls.

docs.title: 3. What are the advantages and disadvantages of automation testing?
docs.text:
Advantages:

  • Faster execution of repetitive tasks.
  • Improved test coverage.
  • Early detection of defects.
  • Reusability of test scripts.
  • Consistent test execution.
  • Efficient regression testing.
  • Increased reliability of test results.

Disadvantages:

  • High initial setup.
  • Maintenance overhead.
  • Inability to replace human intuition.
  • Cost associated with training and resources.

docs.title: 4. When will you avoid automated testing?
docs.text:
1. High Cost of Automation.
  2. Short-Lived or Low-Complexity Projects.
  3. Rapidly Changing Applications.
  4. Non-Repetitive Testing.
  5. Complex Test Scenarios, that are difficult to automate reliably.
  6. Test Data Management Issues: If the application requires complex, large, or dynamic test data that is difficult to manage and maintain in an automated environment.
  7. Data Privacy: If the test data involves sensitive or personal information and handling it securely is challenging.

docs.title: 5. How do you approach writing test scripts for automation?
docs.text:
Writing effective and maintainable test scripts for automation involves a structured approach. Here are the key steps and considerations:

  • Understand Requirements: Clearly understand what needs to be tested and why.
  • Choose Tools: Select appropriate tools and frameworks for the task. (Selenium, Appium, Restsharp)
  • Design Framework: Structure your test automation framework for scalability and maintainability. Create reusable components such as functions, keywords, and data tables to avoid duplication. Design the framework structure, including directories for test cases, keywords, data, and configuration files.
  • Write Scripts: Develop test scripts with clear and reusable components. It should include the necessary setup, actions, and validations.
  • Error Handling: Implement robust error handling (to manage exceptions and unexpected behaviors) and logging (to capture the test execution details, which helps in debugging issues when tests fail.).
  • Manage Data: Use test data from external sources like CSV files, Excel spreadsheets, or databases if your tests require dynamic or varied inputs. If applicable, implement data-driven testing to run the same test logic with different data sets.
  • Integrate CI/CD: Integrate with CI/CD pipelines for automated testing (run tests automatically on code commits or scheduled intervals.).
  • Review and Refactor: Continuously improve and maintain your test scripts.
  • Execute and Monitor: Run and monitor tests to ensure reliability.
  • Document and Train: Provide necessary documentation and training for the team.
  • Reporting: Configure your CI/CD tool to generate and publish test reports, so stakeholders can easily review test results.

docs.title: 6. What strategies do you use to identify areas where automation can improve efficiency or reduce costs?
docs.text: a. Analyze Business Processes: Map processes, document tasks, evaluate repetitive task and evaluate time and resource utilization. b. Gather Feedback: Use surveys and interviews to understand pain points and gather suggestions. c. Evaluate Current Automation: Review existing tools and assess automation coverage. d. Identify Automation Opportunities: Focus on repetitive, high-frequency tasks and perform cost-benefit analysis. e. Pilot and Prototype: Develop prototypes and run pilot programs to validate automation solutions. f. Implement and Monitor: Roll out automation solutions, integrate with existing systems, and continuously monitor and optimize.

docs.title: 7. What strategies do you use to ensure that automated systems remain up-to-date with changing technology?
docs.text: Solution: “I stay informed about industry trends by reading technical blogs, attending webinars, and participating in professional forums. I also regularly review and update the automation tools and frameworks we use to incorporate the latest features and improvements.”

docs.title: 8. What other kinds of testing can be performed on the application?
docs.text:
1. Exploratory testing
  2. Functional testing
  3. Non- functional testing
  4. Performance testing – load testing, stress testing
  5. Security testing
  6. Integration testing

docs.title: 9. How are you going to test an application if no requirement is given and you got the application directly?
docs.text:
1. Will do the exploratory test,
  2. and try to understand the actual flow and functionality working for the application.
  3. Do the documentation and discuss with the application owner if there is any query.

docs.title: 10. What is the difference between Selenium RC and Selenium WebDriver?
docs.text:
• Selenium RC (Remote Control): Older tool that uses a server to inject JavaScript code into web pages to simulate user actions. It is slower and has been largely replaced by WebDriver.
  • Selenium WebDriver: Directly interacts with the browser using its native support, providing faster and more reliable interactions with web elements.

docs.title: 11. How you will prioritize the test Case?
docs.text:
Prioritizing test cases for automation involves determining which test cases should be automated first based on various criteria, including their business value, complexity, and frequency of execution. Here’s a structured approach to prioritize test cases for automation:

  1. Align with Business Objectives: Focus on high-value and compliance-related test cases.
  2. Assess Test Case Characteristics: Prioritize based on frequency of execution, complexity, and stability.
  3. Evaluate Test Case ROI: Perform cost-benefit analysis and consider long-term benefits.
  4. Prioritize Based on Risk: Automate high-risk and historically problematic areas.

  6. Utilize Automation Framework Capabilities: Ensure compatibility and leverage reusable components.
  7. Engage Stakeholders and Review: Gather input from stakeholders and adjust priorities as needed.

docs.title: 13. How would you design a test automation framework from scratch? What components would you include and why?
docs.text:
Designing a test automation framework from scratch requires careful planning and consideration of maintainability, scalability, and efficiency.

  1. Define Framework Goals:

    • Ease of Use: The framework should be easy for both developers and testers to use.
    • Scalability: It should handle the increasing number of tests and growing complexity.
    • Maintainability: Changes in tests or the system under test should not require extensive rework.
    • Modularity and Reusability: Common functionalities should be reusable across different test cases.

  2. Choose the Right Technology Stack:

    • Programming Language: Choose based on the tech stack of the project (e.g., C# for .NET projects, Java for Spring-based projects, Python for data-heavy projects).
    • Automation Tool: Use tools like Selenium, Cypress, or Playwright for UI tests, and RestAssured or Postman for API tests.
    • Test Runner: Use test runners like NUnit (C#), JUnit/TestNG (Java), or PyTest (Python) to organize and execute tests.

  3. Framework Architecture: Design a layered architecture with the following components: 3.1 Test Structure:

    • Test Suites: Organize tests into suites based on functionality, module, or test type (e.g., regression, smoke, unit).
    • Test Cases: Design individual test cases with a single responsibility, focusing on specific functionality.
    • Parameterized Tests: Use data-driven testing to run the same tests with different sets of data (e.g., CSV, JSON, or Excel). 3.2 Page Object Model (POM) for UI Automation:
    • Page Classes: Implement a POM structure where each page or component of the application has a corresponding class. This class contains methods to interact with the page (e.g., click a button, enter text).
    • Advantages: This ensures that UI changes affect only the page classes, not the tests themselves. It also promotes code reuse and separation of concerns. 3.3 Service Layer for API Automation:
    • Service Classes: For API testing, implement service classes to handle HTTP requests and responses.
    • Request Builders: Use a request builder pattern to create complex API requests with different headers, payloads, and parameters.
    • Response Handlers: Implement logic to handle and validate responses, including checking response codes, body content, and headers.

  4. Core Components: 4.1 Test Data Management:

    • Externalize Test Data: Store test data in external files (CSV, JSON, XML, or databases). This allows easy modification of test inputs without changing the test code.
    • Factory Design Pattern: Use factory methods to create objects dynamically based on test data.
    • Randomized Data: If possible, generate randomized data to ensure tests do not rely on hardcoded values. 4.2 Assertion/Validation Layer:
    • Custom Assertion Library: Implement a custom library for common validation tasks (e.g., validating response codes, verifying UI elements, database validation).
    • Soft Assertions: Use soft assertions to continue test execution even if one assertion fails, useful in complex UI tests where you want multiple validations in one run. 4.3 Logging and Reporting:
    • Logger: Integrate a logging framework (e.g., Log4j, Serilog, NLog) to capture runtime information like steps executed, test data, errors, and stack traces.
    • Reporting: Generate reports after each test run using tools like Allure, Extent Reports, or NUnit HTML reports. These should show test results, execution times, and detailed failure logs. 4.4 Test Utilities:
    • Helper Classes: Implement utility classes for common tasks like file reading/writing, API requests, and database queries.
    • Synchronization Methods: Add explicit waits or fluent waits to handle dynamic elements in UI testing.
    • Retry Mechanism: Implement a retry mechanism for flaky tests that may fail due to intermittent issues (e.g., network instability).

  5. Environment and Configuration Management:

    • Environment Profiles: Set up multiple profiles for different environments (development, staging, production). Use environment-specific configurations for URLs, database connections, and credentials.
    • Configuration Files: Store configuration settings in external files (YAML, JSON, or XML). Load them dynamically depending on the environment the tests are running in.

  6. Continuous Integration (CI) Integration:

    • CI Tools: Integrate the framework with CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions). This ensures tests run automatically on every code commit or pull request.
    • Trigger Automated Tests: Set up triggers to run different suites (smoke, regression, nightly) at different stages of the pipeline.
    • Parallel Execution: Configure parallel test execution to reduce runtime using test runners and grid-based tools like Selenium Grid, TestNG, or cloud solutions like BrowserStack.

  7. Parallel and Cross-Browser Testing:

    • Thread-Safe Tests: Ensure tests can run in parallel without conflicting. Use dependency injection or thread-local storage to avoid shared state across threads.
    • Cross-Browser Testing: If testing web apps, set up a mechanism to run tests across different browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) and platforms (Windows, macOS, Linux). Use Selenium Grid or cloud-based services to handle this efficiently.

  8. Version Control and Code Management:

    • Version Control: Store the automation framework in a version control system like Git, enabling collaboration and versioning of the test code.
    • Branching Strategy: Implement a branching strategy (e.g., feature branches, main branch) to ensure code stability and better collaboration between developers and testers.

  9. Scalability and Extensibility:

    • Plugin Support: Ensure the framework is modular enough to support additional plugins use or integrations as needed, like performance testing tools (JMeter, Gatling), security testing (OWASP ZAP), or other utilities.
    • Scalability: Ensure that the framework can handle an increasing number of test cases and run efficiently over time, both in local and CI environments.

  10. Best Practices:

    • Code Reviews: Enforce peer code reviews for tests and framework changes to maintain quality and best practices.
    • Error Handling: Implement robust error handling mechanisms to capture and log exceptions and failures accurately.
    • Test Categorization: Group and tag tests (e.g., smoke, regression, critical) to allow for selective execution based on the situation.
    • Use an repo to store code and commit small small code with proper comment
    • Keep track dependencies and update as needed.
    • Backup your codebase Or use version Control
    • Pom model
    • Logging integration
    • Reporting
    • Documentation
    • Modularizing test script: like payment and user user management
    • Parameterize test data with data table, testsource, data provider

docs.title: 15. Explain the architecture of Selenium WebDriver.
docs.text: Selenium WebDriver follows a client-server architecture. The client (test script) communicates with the WebDriver API, which interacts with different browser drivers to execute commands on the browser.

docs.title: Selenium 3:
docs.text:
Selenium Client Library --> JSON wire protocol over HTTP --> Browser Drivers --> Browsers

  • Selenium Client library: Selenium provides support to multiple libraries such as Ruby, Python, Java, etc as language bindings
  • JSON wire protocol over HTTP: JSON is an acronym for JavaScript Object Notation. It is an open standard that provides a transport mechanism for transferring data between client and server on the web.
  • Browser Drivers: Selenium browser drivers are native to each browser, interacting with the browser by establishing a secure connection. Selenium supports different browser drivers such as ChromeDriver, GeckoDriver, Microsoft Edge WebDriver, SafariDriver, and InternetExplorerDriver.
  • Browsers: Selenium provides support for multiple browsers like Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Internet Explorer etc.

docs.title: Selenium 4:
docs.text:
In Selenium 4, WebDriver W3C Protocol replaces the older JSON Wire protocol. It essentially means that you no longer need to encode and decode the API request using the W3C protocol, and the tests can directly communicate with the web browser.

Selenium Client Library --> WebDriver W3C Protocol --> Browser Drivers --> Browsers

As seen from the architecture of WebDriver W3C Protocol, there is a direct information exchange between the client and server, without the need for the JSON Wire Protocol. As Selenium WebDriver and web browsers use the same protocol, automated Selenium testing will execute tests more consistently between different browsers.

docs.title: 21. Blackbox vs gray box testing.
docs.text:
Black Box testing is the process of testing where tester don’t require the detailed knowledge of or internal structure of application. Testers have no access to the source code or design documents of the mobile app. They test only input and corresponding output response. Example: functionality testing (button, link, menus), Compatibility testing (different devices, OS), Usability Testing (UI, navigation flows).

Grey Box testing: It is a combination of Blackbox testing and white box testing. In this testing process tester has user requirements and documentation of application. Example: Integration testing (how application interact, adding and verifying data in table), Performance testing (speed and response time), Security Testing (encryption and storing the data).

White box testing: software testing technique where the tester has full access to the internal workings of the application's code. It involves looking at the structure of the code. When you know the internal structure of a product, you can conduct tests to ensure that the internal operations are performed according to the specifications. Example: Unit testing(), Path Coverage (every line of code within the sorting algorithm is executed), Performance testing(algorithm's performance with various input sizes), Boundary Testing (how the algorithm handles extreme values)

While executing the selenium test then priority can be selected by:

  2. By setting the priority attribute

docs.title: 23. How to run test case parallelly?
docs.text:
It is a process of running the test case parallel rather than one after another. In parallel testing, the program's multiple parts (or modules) execute together, saving the testers a lot of time and effort.

Nunit:

  • For parallelization, NUnit offers the annotation [Parallelizable] annotation, which can be used at the class level or at the method level.

[TestCase("standard_user"), Order(0), Parallelizable]

  • You can enable parallel execution for all tests in an assembly using the [assembly: Parallelizable]attribute in your AssemblyInfo.cs file:
using NUnit.Framework;
[assembly: Parallelizable(ParallelScope.All)]

When using the [Parallelizable] annotation, we need to specify the scope of the parallelization. Here are the available options:

  • ParallelScope.Self: When the test can run in parallel with other tests. This scope can be applied to classes and methods.
  • ParallelScope.Children: When the child tests can run in parallel with one another. This scope can be applied to the assembly and classes.
  • ParallelScope.Fixtures: When the fixtures (test classes) can run in parallel with one another. This scope applies to the assembly and classes.
  • ParallelScope.All: When the test and its descendants can run in parallel with others at the same level. This scope can be applied to classes and methods.

docs.title: 24. What can be a problem while executing the test case parallel.
docs.text: Concurrency Issues: Tests running in parallel may access shared resources such as databases, files, or network services concurrently. Isolation of Test Data: Tests should ideally be independent and not rely on shared state or global variables. Order Dependency: Some tests may depend on specific execution order or state from preceding tests. Resource Contention: Parallel execution can strain system resources such as CPU, memory, and I/O bandwidth Debugging and Diagnosis: Identifying the root cause of failures or issues in parallel execution can be more challenging compared to sequential execution. Test Environment Setup: Setting up and tearing down test environments (e.g., databases, services) for parallel tests requires careful management to ensure tests start with a clean state and do not interfere with each other.

docs.title: 26. What is the cookies and how we manage in on selenium
docs.text:
In Selenium, cookies represent small pieces of data stored by the browser to remember user-specific information for a particular website, like session details, preferences, or user IDs. Managing cookies in Selenium WebDriver is essential for tasks like maintaining session state across different tests or clearing cookies to simulate a new session.

Using Cookies to Maintain Login State: Here’s an example where we store cookies after logging in, then use them in a subsequent test to avoid logging in again:


// Part 1: Log in and store cookies
IWebDriver driver = new ChromeDriver();
driver.Navigate().GoToUrl("[https://example.com/login](https://example.com/login)");

// Code to perform login
// Assume login is successful

// Store cookies after login
IReadOnlyCollection<Cookie> loginCookies = driver.Manage().Cookies.AllCookies;

// Close the driver after storing cookies
driver.Quit();

// Part 2: Start a new session and reuse cookies
driver = new ChromeDriver();
driver.Navigate().GoToUrl("[https://example.com](https://example.com)");

// Add cookies back to maintain login state
foreach (var cookie in loginCookies)
{
    driver.Manage().Cookies.AddCookie(cookie);
}

// Refresh the page or navigate to another page
driver.Navigate().Refresh();
// Now you’re logged in without needing to log in again

docs.title: 27. How to run the script parallelly on two environments.
docs.text:
Running a Selenium script in parallel across multiple environments (e.g., different browsers or configurations) requires a testing framework that supports parallel execution and, optionally, a test grid for distributing tests across multiple machines.

Configure Tests for Parallel Execution You can use the [Parallelizable] attribute to specify parallel execution. Set up different test methods to run against different environments.


using NUnit.Framework;
using OpenQA.Selenium;
using OpenQA.Selenium.Chrome;
using OpenQA.Selenium.Firefox;

namespace ParallelTests
{
    [TestFixture]
    [Parallelizable(ParallelScope.Children)]
    public class EnvironmentTests
    {
        IWebDriver driver;

        [SetUp]
        public void Setup()
        {
            // Common setup, if any
        }

        [Test]
        [Parallelizable]
        public void TestInChrome()
        {
            driver = new ChromeDriver();
            driver.Navigate().GoToUrl("[https://example.com](https://example.com)");
            // Add your test code here
            Assert.IsTrue(driver.Title.Contains("Example"));
            driver.Quit();
        }

        [Test]
        [Parallelizable]
        public void TestInFirefox()
        {
            driver = new FirefoxDriver();
            driver.Navigate().GoToUrl("[https://example.com](https://example.com)");
            // Add your test code here
            Assert.IsTrue(driver.Title.Contains("Example"));
            driver.Quit();
        }

        [TearDown]
        public void TearDown()
        {
            if (driver != null)
            {
                driver.Quit();
            }
        }
    }
}

docs.title: 30. What is the difference between implicit and explicit waits in Selenium?
docs.text:
• Implicit Wait: Sets a default waiting time for the entire WebDriver instance. If an element is not found immediately, WebDriver will wait for the specified time before throwing an exception. It's set globally for the driver.
using OpenQA.Selenium;
using OpenQA.Selenium.Chrome;

IWebDriver driver = new ChromeDriver();

// Set implicit wait (applies to ALL FindElement calls)
driver.Manage().Timeouts().ImplicitWait = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10);

try 
{
    // This will wait up to 10 seconds if element isn't immediately found
    IWebElement element = driver.FindElement(By.Id("someDynamicElement"));
    element.Click();
}
finally 
{
    driver.Quit();
}
  • Explicit Wait: Waits for a specific condition to be met before proceeding with the next line of code. It waits for a particular element to become visible, clickable, or present, or for any other defined condition. It's used for specific elements and conditions.
using OpenQA.Selenium;
using OpenQA.Selenium.Chrome;
using OpenQA.Selenium.Support.UI; // Required for WebDriverWait

IWebDriver driver = new ChromeDriver();

try 
{
    // Set up explicit wait with 10 second timeout
    WebDriverWait wait = new WebDriverWait(driver, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10));

    // Wait for specific conditions
    IWebElement element = wait.Until(drv => 
    {
        var el = drv.FindElement(By.Id("someDynamicElement"));
        return (el.Displayed && el.Enabled) ? el : null;
    });

    element.Click();

    // Another example - wait for text to contain specific value
    wait.Until(drv => drv.FindElement(By.ClassName("status")).Text.Contains("Complete"));
}
finally 
{
    driver.Quit();
}

docs.title: 31. How do you handle frames or iframes in Selenium?
docs.text:
• Use driver.SwitchTo().Frame() to switch to a frame.
  • You can switch by frame index, name, or WebElement.
  • Use driver.SwitchTo().DefaultContent() to switch back to the main document.
using OpenQA.Selenium;
using OpenQA.Selenium.Chrome;

IWebDriver driver = new ChromeDriver();

try
{
    driver.Navigate().GoToUrl("https://example.com/page-with-frames");

    // Wait for frame to be available (explicit wait)
    WebDriverWait wait = new WebDriverWait(driver, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10));
    IWebElement frame = wait.Until(drv => drv.FindElement(By.Id("contentFrame")));

    // Switch to frame
    driver.SwitchTo().Frame(frame);

    // Now interact with elements inside the frame
    IWebElement searchInput = driver.FindElement(By.Name("search"));
    searchInput.SendKeys("Selenium testing");
    driver.FindElement(By.Id("searchButton")).Click();

    // Switch back to main content
    driver.SwitchTo().DefaultContent();

    // Continue working with main page elements
    driver.FindElement(By.LinkText("Home")).Click();
}
finally
{
    driver.Quit();
}

docs.title: 33. How do you handle multiple windows or tabs in Selenium?
docs.text:
• Use driver.WindowHandles to get a list of all window handles.
  • Use driver.SwitchTo().Window(handle) to switch to a specific window.
  • Use driver.CurrentWindowHandle and driver.getTitle() to verify the current window.
  • Use driver.Close() to close the current window.
  • Use driver.Quit() to close all windows and the WebDriver session.
// Store main window
string mainWindow = driver.CurrentWindowHandle;

// Click button that opens new window
driver.FindElement(By.Id("popupButton")).Click();

// Wait for new window to appear
WebDriverWait wait = new WebDriverWait(driver, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));
wait.Until(drv => drv.WindowHandles.Count == 2);

// Switch to new window
string newWindow = driver.WindowHandles.First(handle => handle != mainWindow);
driver.SwitchTo().Window(newWindow);

// Verify new window content
Assert.IsTrue(driver.Title.Contains("Popup Window"));

// Close popup and return to main
driver.Close();
driver.SwitchTo().Window(mainWindow);

  • StaleWindowHandleException - When window handle becomes invalid
  • TimeoutException - When new window doesn't appear

docs.title: 38. How do you handle scrolling in Selenium?
docs.text:
• Use JavascriptExecutor to execute JavaScript code.
  • Use window.scrollTo(x, y) to scroll to a specific position.

  • Use element.scrollIntoView(true) to scroll to an element.

  • scroll to Element:

using OpenQA.Selenium;
using OpenQA.Selenium.Chrome;

IWebDriver driver = new ChromeDriver();

// Scroll to make element visible
IWebElement element = driver.FindElement(By.Id("footer"));
((IJavaScriptExecutor)driver).ExecuteScript("arguments[0].scrollIntoView(true);", element);

// With smooth scrolling
((IJavaScriptExecutor)driver).ExecuteScript(
    "arguments[0].scrollIntoView({behavior: 'smooth', block: 'center'});", 
    element);
  • Scroll by Pixel Amount:
    // Scroll down by 500 pixels
    ((IJavaScriptExecutor)driver).ExecuteScript("window.scrollBy(0, 500);");
    // Scroll up
    ((IJavaScriptExecutor)driver).ExecuteScript("window.scrollBy(0, -300);");
    // Horizontal scroll
    ((IJavaScriptExecutor)driver).ExecuteScript("window.scrollBy(200, 0);");

  • Example

    ```csharp using OpenQA.Selenium; using OpenQA.Selenium.Chrome; using OpenQA.Selenium.Support.UI;

    class ScrollingExample { public static void Main() { IWebDriver driver = new ChromeDriver();

        try
    {
        driver.Navigate().GoToUrl("https://long-scroll-page.example");

        // Scroll to footer
        WebDriverWait wait = new WebDriverWait(driver, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10));
        IWebElement footer = wait.Until(drv => drv.FindElement(By.Id("page-footer")));

        ((IJavaScriptExecutor)driver).ExecuteScript(
            "arguments[0].scrollIntoView({behavior: 'smooth'});", 
            footer);

        // Scroll up to middle of page
        ((IJavaScriptExecutor)driver).ExecuteScript(
            "window.scrollTo(0, document.body.scrollHeight/2);");

        // Find and click a dynamically loaded element
        IWebElement dynamicElement = wait.Until(drv => 
        {
            ((IJavaScriptExecutor)drv).ExecuteScript("window.scrollBy(0, 100)");
            return drv.FindElement(By.CssSelector(".dynamic-item:visible"));
        });

        dynamicElement.Click();
    }
    finally
    {
        driver.Quit();
    }
}

    } ```

docs.title: input char and wait for suggestion:
docs.text:
• Character-by-character input for reliable triggering
  • Wait for suggestion container before interacting
  • Select suggestions by partial text match
using OpenQA.Selenium;
using OpenQA.Selenium.Chrome;
using OpenQA.Selenium.Support.UI;
using System.Linq;

class FlipkartSearchExample
{
    public static void Main()
    {
        IWebDriver driver = new ChromeDriver();

        try
        {
            // Navigate to Flipkart
            driver.Navigate().GoToUrl("https://www.flipkart.com");

            // Close login popup if present
            try
            {
                driver.FindElement(By.XPath("//button[text()='✕']")).Click();
            }
            catch { /* Popup not present */ }

            // Locate search box
            IWebElement searchBox = new WebDriverWait(driver, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10))
                .Until(drv => drv.FindElement(By.Name("q")));

            // Type search term slowly
            foreach (char c in "air conditioner")
            {
                searchBox.SendKeys(c.ToString());
                Thread.Sleep(100);
            }

            // Wait for suggestions to load
            var wait = new WebDriverWait(driver, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));
            var suggestionsContainer = wait.Until(drv => 
                drv.FindElement(By.CssSelector("._3qX0zy")));

            // Get all suggestions
            var suggestions = suggestionsContainer.FindElements(By.CssSelector("li"));

            // Select suggestion containing "1.5 ton"
            var desiredSuggestion = suggestions.FirstOrDefault(s => 
                s.Text.Contains("1.5 ton") && s.Displayed);

            if (desiredSuggestion != null)
            {
                desiredSuggestion.Click();
            }
            else
            {
                // Fallback: Press Enter for default search
                searchBox.SendKeys(Keys.Enter);
            }

            // Verify search results
            new WebDriverWait(driver, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10))
                .Until(drv => drv.Title.Contains("air conditioner"));
        }
        finally
        {
            driver.Quit();
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Can you tell me Oops concepts and relate it with your Framework?
docs.text: We have Polymorphism, Inheritance, Encapsulation and Abstraction in Oops. So, we will start with:

docs.title: 1) DATA ABSTRACTION
docs.text:
Data Abstraction means to handle complexity by hiding unnecessary details from the user. In java, abstraction is achieved by interfaces and abstract classes. We can achieve 100% abstraction using interfaces.

In Selenium, WebDriver itself acts as an interface. Consider the below statement:

WebDriver driver = new ChromeDriver();

We initialize the Chrome Browser using Selenium Webdriver. It means we are creating a reference variable (driver) of the interface (WebDriver) and creating an Object. Here WebDriver is an Interface and ChromeDriver is a class.

We can apply Data Abstraction in a Selenium framework by using the Page Object Model design pattern. We define all our locators and their methods in the page class. We can use these locators in our tests but we cannot see the implementation of their underlying methods. So we only show the locators in the tests but hide the implementation. This is a simple example of how we can use Data Abstraction in our Automation Framework.

docs.title: 2) ENCAPSULATION
docs.text:
Encapsulation is defined as the wrapping up of data under a single unit. It is the mechanism that binds together code and the data it manipulates. Encapsulation can be achieved by: Declaring all the variables in the class as private and writing public methods in the class to set and get the values of variables.

All the classes in an Automation Framework are an example of Encapsulation. In Page Object Model classes, we declare the data members using @FindBy and initialization of data members will be done using Constructor to utilize those in methods.

docs.title: 3) INHERITANCE
docs.text:
Inheritance is the mechanism in java by which one class is allowed to inherit the features (fields and methods) of another class.

We can apply Inheritance in our Automation Framework by creating a Base Class to initialize the WebDriver interface, browsers, waits, reports, logging, etc. and then we can extend this Base Class and its methods in other classes like Tests or Utilities. This is a simple example of how we can apply Inheritance in our framework.

docs.title: 4) POLYMORPHISM
docs.text:
Polymorphism allows us to perform a single action in different ways. In Java polymorphism can be achieved by two ways:

  • Method Overloading: When there are multiple methods with same name but different parameters then these methods are said to be overloaded. Methods can be overloaded by change in number of arguments or/and change in type of arguments.

In Selenium Automation, Implicit wait is an example of Method Overloading. In Implicit wait we use different time stamps such as SECONDS, MINUTES, HOURS etc.

  • Method Overriding: It occurs when a derived class has a definition for one of the member functions of the base class. That base function is said to be overridden.

In Selenium Automation, Method Overriding can be achieved by overriding any WebDriver method. For example, we can override the findElement method.

In assertion we have used overload because in assertion we used to like asset.true(actual, expected) and second time we can use same assert.true(actual, expected, message).

docs.title: What is Run time polymorphism

docs.title: Abstraction in java and exp?
docs.text: In Page Object Model design pattern, we write locators (such as id, name, xpath etc.,) in a Page Class. We utilize these locators in tests but we can't see these locators in the tests. Literally we hide the locators from the tests.

docs.title: What is the difference between checked and unchecked exceptions?

Checked exceptions: SQLException,IOException,ClassNotFoundException,InvocationTargetException Unchecked exceptions: NullPointerException,ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException,ArithmeticException,IllegalArgumentException, NumberFormatException

docs.title: Apart from sendkeys, are there any different ways, to type content onto the editable field?

docs.title: What are hashmap and HashSet? Explain?
docs.text: HashMap and HashSet both are one of the most important classes of Java Collection framework. HashMap Stores elements in form of key-value pair i.e each element has its corresponding key which is required for its retrieval during iteration. HashSet stores only objects no such key value pairs maintained.

docs.title: Where do you use a hashmap?
docs.text:
Maps are used for when you want to associate a key with a value and Lists are an ordered collection. Map is an interface in the Java Collection Framework and a HashMap is one implementation of the Map interface. HashMap are efficient for locating a value based on a key and inserting and deleting values based on a key.

HashMap<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();

// Add elements to the map 
map.put("vishal", 10); 
map.put("sachin", 30); 
map.put("vaibhav", 20); 

// Print size and content 
System.out.println("Size of map is:- " + map.size()); 
System.out.println(map); 

// Check if a key is present and if present, print value 
if (map.containsKey("vishal")) { 
    Integer a = map.get("vishal"); 
    System.out.println("value for key \"vishal\" is:- " + a); 
}

docs.title: What is a singleton class?
docs.text: The Singleton's purpose is to control object creation, limiting the number of objects to only one. Since there is only one Singleton instance, any instance fields of a Singleton will occur only once per class, just like static fields. Singletons often control access to resources, such as database connections or sockets.

docs.title: JAVA ONE LINE CONCEPTS
docs.text:
• java file mai ek hi public class hoti hai, uske alava aur classes v ho sakti hai par public ek hi.
  • If we need to create one variable for multiple values, we need to use Array concept.
  • Int marks[] = new int[5]
  • Array can store only homogenous data, int for int array, string for string.
  • If we need to add heterogeneous data in array, we need to create object array.
  • Object a[] = new Object[5]; now we can add different data type objects.
  • Array is fixed in size, which we define while creating.
  • If we try to access index value >= given index value, we got arrayOutOfBundException.
  • Arrays are not defined by any data layer structure so we can't run readymade methods on it.
  • To overcome this, we have collection framework under which there are ArrayList, List, HashMap, HashTable, Tree, Stack.
  • We can add new elements in run time under collections while in array we cannot.
  • Collection is a group of objects. To represent this we need certain interfaces and classes.
  • Common operations we generally do on collections are adding objects, removing objects & finding object.
  • Collection (I) is called collection interface having methods which are common throughout all collections.
  • Collections is basically a class from java.util package which contains some methods which we can use for collection objects.
  • Collection - 1. List, 2. Set, 3. Queue
  • List (I) is child of collection(I). In list Insertion order is preserved and duplicates are allowed.
  • ArrayList, LinkedList, Vector these are different classes which implements List Interface.
  • Set(I) is child of collection(I). Insertion order is not preserved & duplicates not allowed.
  • HashSet, Linked Hashset these are different classes which implements Set Interface.
  • Queue(I) is child of collection(I). We used it when we need prior to processing means first in first out concept.
  • priorityQueue is class which implements Set Interface.
  • There is one independent interface known as Map(I). In Map(I) objects are created with key and value pair. Key cannot be duplicate, but Value can be.
  • Hashmap, Linked Hashmap, Hash Table these are different classes which implements Map Interface.
  • Whatever methods present in Collection(I) are also present in their child interface i.e List, Set, Queue.
  • add(object o), addAll(Collection c), remove(Object o), removeAll(Collection c), retainAll(Collection c) these are some methods of Collection Interface.
  • clear(), isEmpty(), size(), contains(), conatinsAll(), toArray() are also some methods.
  • In List index play an important role because with the help of index only we can find duplicates elements.
  • add(index , object), get(index), set(index, object) are methods of List Interface.
  • ArrayList al= new ArrayList(), it allows heterogenous objects also.
  • ArrayList al= new (), now it can store objects of string only.
  • Collections.Sort(al), Collections.Shuffle(al) This will sort & shuffle the objects of arraylist.
  • We can read the data with for loop, for each loop, iterator () method.
  • JVM have 2 types of memories Static pool -static data, heaps-Non static data.

  • Static methods are accessed by class, Non Static methods are accessed by objects.
  • Constructor in java is to make objects, we can create constructor but there is one default constructor in java, like students a = new students(); highlighted is the default constructor.
  • Constructor are non static methods. Constructor can be parameterized.
  • We can create our own constructor like students b= new students(int rollNo ,String name){}
  • this() keyword is used to call one constructor by another.
  • this() keyword also used in agar 2 alag alag methods mai same parameter name hai , to conflict na ho isliye this.name, this.rollNo use krte h. this is known as method overloading bcs you are using one method parameter in second one.
  • Inheritance ka matlab hai ki Parent class ki property ko hum child class mai bhi use kar sake.
  • e.g class Sci extends students{}, extends keyword ki help se hum students class ki property ko Sci class mai inherit kr rahe h.
  • super() keyword parent class ke constructor ko child mai le ata hai , means ab agar hum Sci class ka object baneyenge to students class ka v ek object banega.
